title: Cattle, Wealth, and Responsibility
subtitle: True wealth is measured not only by what a person owns, but by how responsibly it is protected and used.
author: Murle Connect Editorial Team
proverb: Wealth without responsibility becomes a burden instead of a blessing.
summary: This proverb reflects the importance of cattle and livestock within traditional livelihood, family obligations, social relationships, and community life. It teaches that ownership brings responsibility, and wealth becomes meaningful only when it is protected, shared wisely, and used to support family and community well-being.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Among the Murle people, cattle have traditionally held deep economic, social, and cultural importance. They provide wealth, support family life, contribute to marriage arrangements, strengthen relationships, and connect generations. However, owning cattle is not simply a sign of status. It also requires knowledge, patience, protection, care, and responsibility. This proverb reminds people that wealth has value only when it is managed wisely.

sections.heading: Meaning
sections.content: The proverb teaches that possessions alone do not make a person successful. A person may own many cattle or other forms of wealth, but if they are careless, selfish, wasteful, or irresponsible, that wealth can create problems. Wealth should be protected, used carefully, and directed toward meaningful responsibilities. True prosperity includes the ability to care for dependents, support relatives, plan for the future, and maintain peace.

sections.heading: Traditional Story
sections.content: A wealthy cattle owner once became proud of the size of his herd and stopped listening to experienced herders. He neglected the animals, failed to prepare for difficult seasons, and refused to share assistance with relatives facing hardship. Over time, disease, drought, and poor management reduced his herd. Another cattle keeper with fewer animals survived because he cared for them carefully, sought advice, shared responsibilities, and prepared for difficult conditions. The story teaches that responsible management is more important than appearance or quantity.

sections.heading: Lesson
sections.content: The proverb teaches stewardship. Wealth should not produce arrogance or disregard for others. It should encourage gratitude, careful planning, generosity, and responsibility. Cattle require daily attention, and the same principle applies to money, education, land, businesses, relationships, and opportunities. Anything valuable can be lost when it is treated carelessly.

sections.heading: Modern Application
sections.content: Today, the proverb applies beyond cattle to salaries, businesses, education, technology, property, and financial resources. A person who earns money but spends it without planning may remain insecure. A person who receives education but refuses to help others may fail to create wider benefit. Communities can apply this lesson by managing resources transparently, supporting vulnerable families, investing in children’s education, and using wealth to build lasting opportunities rather than temporary prestige.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Wealth is a responsibility before it is a privilege. Cattle, money, land, knowledge, and influence become blessings when they are protected and used with wisdom. The proverb reminds people that prosperity should strengthen families, preserve dignity, support community life, and prepare future generations. Ownership without responsibility is fragile, but responsible stewardship creates lasting value.

moral: Wealth becomes meaningful when it is managed responsibly, protected carefully, and used to support family and community.
reflection: How are you using the resources, skills, or opportunities you currently possess to benefit others?
